texts.orig: Q: My company is constantly going through reorgs. It stresses me out. Partly because I can never feel fully settled, and partly because I feel like I should be taking advantage these opportunities to move ahead in my career. Any advice?
texts.text: Q: My company is constantly going through reorgs. It stresses me out. Partly because I can never feel fully settled, and partly because I feel like I should be taking advantage these opportunities to move ahead in my career. Any advice?

texts.orig: Reorgs are a way of life at fast-growing startups, and if you ask me, they’re a good thing. Competitors make moves, markets shift, and new information emerges. It’s important for your business to adapt. Would you rather your company just keep doing what it’s been doing because it’s easy? I wouldn’t.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: On an individual level, as you suggested, reorgs are a great opportunity to take a step forward in your career. Some of the biggest jumps in my own career have come as a result of reorgs. The changing team structures often unlock new opportunities, new leadership roles, and if nothing else give you a chance to take on more responsibility. So it’s wise to think ahead.

texts.orig: I believe one of the most important things we can have in life is a sense of humor. The word “humor” has the same root as “humus” (earth), “human”, and “humility.” Having a sense of humor about ourselves and life grounds us, makes us more human and connected, and humbles us. Humor helps us relax, become more creative, absorb new ideas and learn better. It grants us acceptance that things are as they are, which serves as a springboard for change. texts.orig: On a light note, here’s some final great advice from Bruce Lee. He deeply understood constant change and evolution and his philosophy is now more valuable than ever. The rigor of Lee's daily discipline and continuous improvement allowed him to let go and flow. Your new habits around perspective, self-reflection, relationships, mindfulness - and humor, will help you do the same.
